title: An arbitrary compact-support isomorphism can destroy a trace pairing
statement: For every nontrivial commutative ring A there is an A-linear automorphism e of A×A such that sum(e(x))=x₁ for every x. Consequently sum(e(h·(0,1)))=0 for all h although (0,1) is nonzero. This is the elementary two-component normalization test for the pairing in [lem-coef-tower-natural-currying].

source.place: Elementary linear-algebra test of the finite counit pairing in paragraph 2.

proof.text: Use e(x,y)=(x-y,y) with inverse (x,y)=(x+y,y). The coordinate sum is x. The product h·(0,1) has first coordinate zero, and the second basis vector is nonzero by nontriviality. The formulas use no division and include characteristic two.

lean.statement:
theorem coefCurrying_trace_twist (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [Nontrivial A] :
    ∃ e : (A × A) ≃ₗ[A] (A × A),
      (∀ x : A × A, (e x).1 + (e x).2 = x.1) ∧
      (0, 1) ≠ (0 : A × A) ∧
      ∀ h : A × A,
        (e (h.1 * 0, h.2 * 1)).1 + (e (h.1 * 0, h.2 * 1)).2 = 0
